selected_evidence.summary: Shows the installed PAM, systemd-manager, and sysctl policies.

selected_evidence.requirement: Core dumps disabled while normal crash logging remains
selected_evidence.summary: The nobody service had LimitCORE=0, could not raise it, created zero core artifacts, and its SIGSEGV was recorded by journald and /var/log/messages.

Healthy baseline boot ID 192f6cab-c39d-4e64-a3f6-50e677966ca2, acknowledged reboot, changed boot ID 76e4ea0b-4a71-473c-9031-2a2588d26729, active journald/rsyslog/sshd, zero failed units, persisted limits, and a successful post-restart crash test with logging but no core file.

# Disable core files for all PAM-managed local accounts.
* soft core 0
* hard core 0
# Disable core files for processes started by the service manager.
[Manager]
DefaultLimitCORE=0:0
# Do not dump memory from set-user-ID or otherwise privileged processes.
fs.suid_dumpable = 0

sudo tee /usr/local/sbin/core-limit-postboot-probe >/dev/null <<'ANTRIEB_SCRIPT'
#!/bin/sh
grep '^Max core file size' /proc/self/limits > limits.before
if ulimit -c unlimited 2> raise.err; then
  printf 'unexpected_success\n' > raise.result
else
  printf 'blocked\n' > raise.result
fi
grep '^Max core file size' /proc/self/limits > limits.after
exec /usr/bin/python -c 'import os, signal; os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGSEGV)'
ANTRIEB_SCRIPT
sudo chmod 0755 /usr/local/sbin/core-limit-postboot-probe
sudo tee /run/systemd/system/core-limit-postboot-probe.service >/dev/null <<'ANTRIEB_UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=Post-restart core limit and crash logging verification

[Service]
Type=simple
User=nobody
Group=nobody
WorkingDirectory=/var/tmp/core-limit-postboot-probe
ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/core-limit-postboot-probe
ANTRIEB_UNIT
sudo chmod 0644 /run/systemd/system/core-limit-postboot-probe.service
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl cat core-limit-postboot-probe.service
